git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ shows, inside this case's list, only the do: rule rewritten (SKILL.md) and an example change under Write module names literally in macros.md (the two one-line for comprehensions became for ... do ... end blocks; the rule's sentences are unchanged). Add specs, and hide technical functions from the docs and the other five macros.md rules are unchanged and are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-23/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json: validation in a @doc false function called from a one-line quote is clean under Keep quote blocks small, and a route recorded by a direct attribute write inside get's quote is violated even when validation runs outside quote (the standard in every earlier sweep); the use documentation rule needs an admonition at the top of @moduledoc, and effects stated in prose without one are violated (as in 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22-b); __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them (Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden for every __ function and macro in all four runs); a guard-wrapped one-expression block whose do: form is a judgement call is not counted. The other rewordings of this round (the named-argument rule, the pipeline rule's one-line sentence, the capture rule's placeholder-order sentence) and the new -> clause rule are outside this case's list and appear only under other_violations.

Do: rule, graded against the current text, per sentence. Sentence 1 (Use `do:` for a body of one expression with no body of its own inside it: a literal, a tuple, a field read, a comparison, or a call, nested or not) decides all four clean verdicts: every do: body is a literal, a tuple or a call (haiku-1 lines 42, 45, 65, 90-91, 100, 110; haiku-2 lines 59, 107, 117, 119, 121-122, 124; sonnet-1 lines 68, 111, 113-114, 123, 134; sonnet-2 lines 69, 77, 112, 122, 124). fn sentence and capture sentence (A capture that carries a call with arguments of its own ... is a second body too): 0 of 4; the fn and argument-carrying captures sit in block bodies or bindings, never in a do: body (haiku-1 line 38 fn and line 62 &match_route(&1, segments); haiku-2 line 88 &match_route(&1, segments); sonnet-1 line 104 fn; sonnet-2 line 87 fn). if sentence (`if ..., do: ..., else: ...` stays on one line when one branch is a name or a literal): no one-line if in any run; only haiku-2 has an if (lines 131-135), a block with :ok and a call whose one-line form would not fit, so it is clean. for sentence (A `for` always takes `do ... end`): not exercised, no for in any file. Mix sentence: 0 of 4 broken; every mixed function sets block clauses apart with a blank line. Head's-line sentence: no do: body on a line of its own in any file. Every one-expression do ... end block joins to more than 98 characters (haiku-1 111-146, haiku-2 104-146, sonnet-1 99-146, sonnet-2 119-143), so none could be a do: line; guard-wrapped blocks (haiku-1 lines 71-74, sonnet-1 lines 85-88 and 129-132, sonnet-2 lines 95-98) are the allowed wrap's alternative and are not counted.

Pipeline rule (outside the list), current text: the sentence A pipeline never sits on one line, however short decides haiku-1 line 37 (two steps after env.module on one line, as in 2026-10-23) and sonnet-1 line 108 (a two-step pipeline inside a tuple). haiku-2, sonnet-1 (lines 58-61) and sonnet-2 (lines 61-64) write the same __before_compile__ pipeline on three lines. Named-argument rule (outside the list), current text: no run passes a multi-line map, struct or non-trailing keyword list as an argument and no literal has more than six elements; haiku-1 line 81 and haiku-2 line 143 pass trailing keyword lists to raise on one line, which the trailing keyword list sentence allows. Capture rule (outside the list), current text: the placeholder-order sentence is not broken; both argument captures (&match_route(&1, segments)) use &1 once. No -> clause passes 70 characters in any run.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace, one scratch Mix project per run (the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex, plus real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules). haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 report alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime) and alias MyApp.UserHandler (runtime); they call Macro.expand_literals in get with {:call, 2} (haiku-2) or {:match, 1} (sonnet-1, sonnet-2). haiku-1 never expands the handler and passes the alias into a call in the router's module body, and xref reports lib/tiny_router.ex:116: alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile) and lib/tiny_router.ex:117: alias MyApp.UserHandler (compile). All four compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3).

Bad-declaration checks: each project loaded with mix run, then Code.compile_string compiled one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one declaring get "/", "not a module". All eight fail while the router compiles: haiku-1 and haiku-2 with CompileError (nofile:3: route path must be a string, got: 123; handler must be a module name, got: "not a module"), raised from __define__/4; sonnet-1 with ArgumentError from __define__/3; sonnet-2 with ArgumentError from validate_route!/2 during macro expansion (route path must be a string literal, got: 123).

Format: haiku-1 and sonnet-2 pass mix format --check-formatted as delivered (both accepted parentheses on the two get calls). sonnet-1 wrote a .formatter.exs with locals_without_parens: [get: 2] and export, and passes with it. haiku-2 fails (format_ok false): mix format changes only the two get calls at lines 150-151 to parentheses; the run saw that diff at its first check and delivered the file unchanged. haiku-2 also left four scratch scripts (zz_check_bad_handler.exs, zz_check_bad_path.exs, zz_check_behave.exs, zz_debug.exs) in its output folder after the permission system blocked their removal; they are test scripts, not graded.

Reads: all four read SKILL.md, macros.md and library-design.md before writing tiny_router.ex. haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 used one Read call per file; haiku-1 read SKILL.md with Read and both reference files with cat in one Bash call. This matches result.json reads and satisfies the Expected reads line.

Against 2026-10-23's skill runs: the do: rule stays clean on Haiku and Sonnet under the rewritten text. Keep quote blocks small moves from clean to violated on Sonnet (sonnet-2 records with a direct attribute write and validates in the macro body). The compile-time-dependency rule moves from clean to violated on Haiku (haiku-1 drops Macro.expand_literals). The use documentation rule stays violated on Haiku (haiku-1 states the effects in prose with no admonition; in 2026-10-23 haiku-1 placed its admonition after a Usage example). The other four rules stay clean on both tiers. The one-line __before_compile__ pipeline appears in one haiku run (two in 2026-10-23).

Smoke test outside the rules: all four return routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/" with string param keys (%{"id" => "42"}), and return :error for "/nope" and "/users". All four match at runtime through a @doc false __match__/2.
